title: System Monitor
summary: A live look at the Raspberry Pi it runs on: CPU, temperature, memory, storage, network, processes and the power supply.
description: A full-screen monitor of the board it runs on, made for the deck's small screen and for touch. The overview is a grid of six tiles that fills the screen: Power first, in plain words and colours (Power OK in green; under-voltage now in red with 'check the power supply'; under-voltage, throttling or frequency capping since boot in amber, with the time since boot of the last event), CPU load, temperature (amber from 70 °C, red from 80 °C, where the Pi starts to slow down), memory, the space used on the system disk and the network (address, in and out rates, Wi-Fi signal), each with a history line of the last two minutes. A tap on a tile (or Enter on the tile with the ring) opens its page with a live chart and the details: each core, frequency, load and the top processes by CPU; memory with the top processes by memory; temperature and power (each firmware flag, the fan, the 5 V input on a Pi 5); every disk and its read/write rate; every network interface with its address, rates and Wi-Fi signal. A Processes page lists the top 15 by CPU or by memory; a System page names the model, kernel, OS and firmware and shows the app's own CPU and memory. Values refresh every 1, 2 or 5 seconds (remembered). Read-only: it changes nothing on the system. Works on the Pi Zero 2 W, Pi 3A+, Pi 5 and CM5; the firmware flags need vcgencmd and the video group (without them the rest works). Needs a screen of at least 640x480 and a launcher with full-screen app support.
